questions.q: The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends exclusively breastfeeding for the first 6 months. During this period, which supplement is routinely recommended for breastfed infants to prevent rickets?
questions.explain: Breast milk is low in Vitamin D. The AAP recommends a supplement of 400 IU of Vitamin D daily for exclusively breastfed infants.

questions.q: A mother asks when she should introduce solid foods to her infant. Which of the following developmental signs indicates the infant is ready for complementary foods?
options: The infant can roll over from back to front
The infant has tripled their birth weight
The extrusion (tongue-thrust) reflex has diminished and the infant can sit with support
The infant sleeps through the night without waking
questions.explain: Physiological readiness for solids (typically 4-6 months) is marked by the disappearance of the extrusion reflex (which pushes food out) and the ability to hold the head up and sit with support.

questions.q: Why is cow's milk NOT recommended for infants under 1 year of age?
options: It contains insufficient calcium for bone growth
It has a high renal solute load and can cause intestinal bleeding
It contains too much Vitamin C, leading to toxicity
It lacks the protein casein needed for muscle development
questions.explain: Cow's milk contains high protein and mineral levels (high renal solute load) that stress immature kidneys and can cause GI bleeding/iron deficiency. It is also low in iron and Vitamin C.

questions.q: A 9-month-old infant is being fed a variety of table foods. Which food should be strictly avoided due to the risk of botulism?
questions.explain: Honey may contain *Clostridium botulinum* spores, which can colonize an infant's immature gut and cause botulism.

questions.q: An infant is diagnosed with 'Failure to Thrive' (FTT). Which of the following is an **organic** cause of FTT?
options: Lack of nutritional knowledge by caregivers
questions.explain: Organic FTT is caused by an underlying medical condition (like Cystic Fibrosis or CHD). The other options are non-organic (environmental/psychosocial) causes.

questions.q: An infant is born prematurely at 32 weeks gestation. Which reflex is most likely to be underdeveloped, potentially interfering with oral feeding?
questions.explain: The coordination of sucking, swallowing, and breathing typically matures around 34 weeks gestation. Premature infants often require tube feeding until this skill is acquired.

options: Its composition remains exactly the same from birth to weaning
It contains only water and lactose
Its composition changes during a feed (foremilk vs hindmilk) and over time to meet the infant's needs
It is always identical between different mothers
questions.explain: Breast milk changes from colostrum to mature milk, and during a single feed (foremilk is watery, hindmilk is fat-rich), adapting to the baby's hydration and energy needs.
